key_insight: Experience Memory Graph turns agent failure recovery into graph matching, letting LLM agents correct mistakes in one shot instead of relying on brittle iterative reflection loops.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more scalable and lower-latency way to make autonomous agents robust on long-horizon tasks, reducing test-time API cost and trial-and-error overhead.
method: Convert failed and successful trajectories into directed action decision graphs.
Match graphs to extract successful subgraphs and explicit edit paths for correction.
Store reusable intra-task nodes and cross-task edges in a memory graph for retrieval at test time.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld show EMG improves success rate and average reward over reflection baselines while avoiding test-time trial-and-error.
watch_item: Graph construction and matching may be sensitive to trajectory quality and task format, so generalization across very different environments could require careful engineering.
paper_title: Experience Memory Graph: One-Shot Error Correction for Agents
